source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Chandler campus is the largest published data center load in Arizona at 169 MW, and it is the only reason the state's disclosed total reaches 512.02 MW.

The concentration is an artifact of disclosure, not of construction. Arizona has 57 mapped facilities, and only four publish a megawatt figure at all. One campus holding a third of the state's published capacity says more about which operators report numbers than about where the state's actual load sits. The 169 MW spans eight buildings, PHX1 through PHX8, and 2 million square feet of technical space, so the figure is a campus total rather than a single hall.

The data does not include an address or postal code, so the physical siting is not stated. It also does not include rack counts or accelerator counts, which means any translation of 169 MW into hardware requires an assumption the operator has not made. At 40 kW per rack the load implies roughly 4,225 racks, and at 10 kW per rack roughly 16,900, but neither is CyrusOne's claim and the real fit-out is unpublished.

The certifications describe what classes of work the campus is eligible to host, not who hosts it. SOC 1 and SOC 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, TIA-942, and Green Globes each cover a different domain, from financial controls to federal systems to physical telecommunications infrastructure. No tenant is named, and a certification is not evidence of a particular tenant.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
